questions.a: It means managing reviews and ratings store by store, instead of only at the brand level. Each location has its own customers, service moments and online reviews, and that's what nearby searchers see. Tracking each store separately shows you where to coach, where to invest and which issues to fix first.

questions.q: How do Google reviews affect a restaurant location's ranking?
questions.a: Google's local ranking weighs relevance, distance and prominence, and prominence is tied to review count, score and recency. A location with more recent, higher-rated reviews tends to appear in the Map Pack more often for "near me" searches. That can hold true even between two stores of the same brand.

questions.q: Why do a few low-rated stores matter for a multi-location brand?
questions.a: Low-rated stores drag down how people see the whole brand, get buried in search results and wear down loyalty among guests who do visit. They often need costly service recovery once the damage is done. Even if most of your locations perform well, a few stores under 4.0 stars can hold back your growth.

questions.q: How can I improve ratings across all my restaurant locations?
questions.a: Use a tool that pulls reviews from every platform and location together, then break the insights down by store. Reply to reviews with personalized messages, set alerts for negative trends and track which locations are improving or slipping. Then go beyond replying by recovering unhappy guests and fixing the issues they raise.
